sections.h2: Where does a Carteret County deed get filed?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds takes deeds in the County Administrative Building, which stands at 302 Courthouse Square in Beaufort. Anyone can inspect records there on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.

The office calls itself the legal custodian of every land record and land transaction in the county, and it indexes and images each one into the permanent file. The county says the whole file is open to the public except military discharges. An online database lets you view and print land records from home, which is the fastest route to your vesting deed before listing.

One detail applies to older paperwork. The county's real estate page says Books 301 through 514 are on aperture cards, and a cancelled deed of trust is stamped on the card itself. If you need proof that an old loan was released and the online image does not show it, call the office rather than assuming the lien is still open.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Carteret County?
sections.html:
The county publishes one fee list, and its real estate lines track the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10. The office accepts cash, credit or debit card, money orders and cashier's checks for recording.

Document or serviceFee as the county prints it
General instruments other than deeds of trust and mortgages$26 covers 15 pages, then $4 a page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64 covers 35 pages, then $4 a page
Plats$21 per sheet
Satisfaction instrumentsNo fee per statute
Document containing multiple instrumentsAdditional $10
Nonstandard documentsAdditional $25
Certified copies$5 for page one, $2 per page after
Uncertified copies$0.25
Excise tax valuation$2 per $1000.00 of sales price

On the same list, each added index reference on an assignment adds $10 and a military discharge is recorded free. The page carries an October 1, 2019 effective date, so ask the office whether any line has changed since then.

sections.h2: How do I keep a Carteret County deed from being charged as nonstandard?
sections.html:
Follow the county's published recording standards, because a document that misses them is still recorded but costs an extra $25. The office's penalty paragraph says it will record the nonconforming document after collecting the $25 nonstandard fee along with the normal recording fee.

  • Page size: letter or legal.
  • First page: leave 3 inches blank across the top.
  • Remaining sides of page one and all sides of later pages: a 1/4 inch blank margin, per the standards page.
  • Print: black on white, in a legible font, with 10 points as the smallest size treated as legible.
  • Pages: one-sided only.
  • Title: name the kind of instrument at the head of page one.

The fee page contradicts the standards page on side margins. It says the minimum side margin went back to one-half inch under Session Law 2019-117, effective October 1, 2019, while the standards page still shows 1/4 inch. Ask the office which one it applies before you print the deed. Pen is acceptable for blanks and corrections, and the office may treat slightly small type as legible and skip the fee.

sections.h2: Who owes the stamp tax when a Carteret County house sells?
sections.html:
The seller owes it. As G.S. 105-228.30 reads, the transferor pays the register of deeds before the deed goes on record.

In the statute the rate is $1.00 for each $500.00, and a leftover fraction counts as a full unit. Carteret County's fee page expresses the same thing as $2 per $1000.00 of the sales price. On a settlement statement it shows on the seller's side, since the closing agent usually withholds it from the proceeds.

Filing matters as much as the tax. Per G.S. 47-18, a transfer is ineffective against lien creditors and paying purchasers until it is registered in the county of the land. A buyer who does not record leaves the door open to later claims.

sections.h2: What should I pull from the Carteret County records before listing?
sections.html:
Pull four items from the online database or the Beaufort counter: your vesting deed, every deed of trust that touches the parcel and its release if one exists, any plat for the lot, and recorded easements. Plats are priced by the sheet, at $21 each on the county's fee list, and map copies are $1.00 or $2.00 depending on size.

  • The vesting deed shows exactly how title is held, including any co-owners who must sign.
  • A recorded satisfaction shows that an old loan was released, and the county charges nothing to file one.
  • A plat or map tells you the lot lines before a buyer's survey does.
  • Uncertified copies cost $0.25 a page, so printing the record for your own file is cheap.

A recorded release is the proof a title company looks for. If the loan is paid and no release shows, ask the lender to file one rather than waiting for the buyer's title search to find the gap.

sections.h2: How do Carteret County property taxes figure into a sale?
sections.html:
Whatever tax is still open on the parcel gets paid out of the closing, so phone the Tax Administration Office on 252-728-8485 for the amount well ahead of the settlement table. That office sits in the same Beaufort building as the register of deeds, which makes it easy to handle both errands in one trip.

The register and the tax office do different jobs. The register records the deed and collects the stamp tax. The tax office bills the annual tax, hears value questions and tracks relief claims. Our Carteret County property tax guide covers due dates, interest, appeals and collection steps in detail.

sections.h2: What other papers does the Carteret County office handle for an inherited house?
sections.html:
Birth, death and marriage records for events in the county are also kept here, with certified copies available. The fee page prices a certified death certificate and a certified marriage license copy at $10 each, and notes that not everyone may obtain a certified copy, so confirm eligibility first.

An heir selling a parent's house would normally gather the death certificate, the vesting deed and certified copies of recorded papers touching the land; those copies run $5 for page one and $2 for each page after. If an estate is involved, ask the Carteret County Clerk of Superior Court what the estate file requires.

The office describes itself as a recording office, so it gives no legal advice, supplies no legal forms and will not explain the legal effect of an instrument. Use an attorney for drafting.

sections.h2: How big is the Carteret County housing market?
sections.html:
The land area is 507.60 square miles, and the Census estimate for July 2025 is 70,469 people, up 4.1% from the 2020 base. The Census counts 54,293 housing units against 31,977 households for 2020-2024, so the county has well over 20,000 more homes than households.

  • The median owned home was worth $333,300 over 2020-2024, and owners occupy 74.7% of units.
  • Median gross rent: $1,108.
  • Median household income: $72,322.
  • Residents 65 and over: 30.1%.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 471.
  • Persons per household: 2.13; households 31,977.

Those figures are from the Census QuickFacts page. If you own here but live elsewhere, documents can be mailed to the Beaufort address above, and the county's online database lets you check the record from a distance.

faqs.q: Will Carteret County charge me to file a release after I pay off my mortgage?
faqs.a: No. The county's fee page lists satisfaction instruments at no fee per statute, so paying off a loan does not cost anything to record the release.

faqs.q: What does a standard Carteret County deed cost to file?
faqs.a: Expect $26 through page 15, then $4 per added page. A deed that breaks the layout standards adds $25, and a document that bundles several instruments adds $10.

faqs.q: How can I pay for recording at the Carteret County register of deeds?
faqs.a: Bring cash, a card, a money order or a cashier's check. Mail can be sent to 302 Courthouse Square, Beaufort, NC 28516.

faqs.q: Can I view Carteret County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says land records can be viewed and printed from its Register of Deeds Online Database. Books 301 through 514 are on aperture cards, so call the office about cancellation details for those older records.

faqs.q: What is the Carteret County transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: The county lists it as $2 per $1000.00 of the sales price, the same as the state's $1.00 per $500.00, and the seller pays it before filing.
